gate_reasoning: Stage 4 scores 28% High / 41% Medium / 31% Low across 32 claims. The high-confidence backbone is solid: Chubb Life's PwC-audited OJK filing, Milliman's Indonesia newsletter with verbatim cached health claims data, Swiss Re's protection gap PDF, and three peer-reviewed academic sources all hold at High. The Low cluster is dominated by three structural problems: (1) all five insurer-programme capability claims sourced from vendor marketing pages or press releases trigger auto-Low per vendor-marketing override — this is expected and correct for a stage where primary evidence of programme absence is itself the finding; (2) the AXA Mandiri premium/lives figure relies solely on Heaptalk; (3) the Indonesia-wide health claims aggregate and loss ratio both need their primary chain (AAJI statistics, OJK Insurance Statistics, or WTW direct report) fetched to reach Medium or High. Six targeted deep-research actions can elevate four Low claims to Medium or High. The core analytical finding — zero operational CDM programmes across all five insurers — is robust and supported by absence of counter-evidence across primary-filing and ministry sources. Ship with flag pending deep-research on AXA financials, AAJI aggregate claims, WTW loss ratio, and Prudential Indonesia health sub-claims.
